summary: At just 1.6 square miles and roughly 2,300 residents, Ross is essentially a single wooded neighborhood tucked into the floor of a narrow Marin County valley, where mature redwoods and live oaks canopy winding lanes with no sidewalks, no commercial district, and no traffic lights. The town sits along Corte Madera Creek at the base of Mount Tamalpais, which means trail access to thousands of acres of open space is measured in minutes on foot, not by car — yet Highway 101 is close enough to make a San Francisco commute viable, if painful during peak hours. This is almost purely a bedroom community; there is no meaningful employment base within the town itself, so the median household income topping $250,000 is earned elsewhere, largely in San Francisco's financial and professional sectors or across Marin's healthcare and education institutions. With a median home value exceeding $2 million and median rent above $3,400, the price-to-income ratio is roughly eight-to-one — steep even for top earners. Average daily highs hover around 66°F year-round with nine hours of sunshine, meaning the mild, marine-influenced climate rarely forces anyone indoors. Ross is a place where the extraordinary natural setting and the extraordinary cost of entry are essentially the same fact.
